critical.issue: Withdrawal is invisible to the read side. Sort is by granted_at DESC, but withdrawal rows have granted_at=None, so they sort last. After POST /consents/marketing_comms then DELETE /consents/marketing_comms, GET still reports status='granted'. Fix: sort by a unified timestamp — e.g. add COALESCE(granted_at, withdrawn_at) or store an 'event_ts' field on every row and sort by that.

rca of the issue: Consent withdrawal read-bug RCA: withdraw() inserts row with granted_at=None, withdrawn_at=NOW(). current_for_user() does .sort('granted_at', -1) — MongoDB sorts nulls last in DESC order. First match per purpose becomes the earlier grant row. User sees status='granted' even after successful withdraw. Repro: POST /api/compliance/consents/marketing_comms → 200 granted. DELETE /api/compliance/consents/marketing_comms → 200 withdrawn. GET /api/compliance/consents → marketing_comms status STILL 'granted' (should be 'withdrawn'). Fix: change sort to use an event_ts field populated on both grant and withdraw paths (e.g. event_ts = granted_at or withdrawn_at at insert).
